source.name: FY 2026 HUD Income Limits Area Definitions
HUD FY2026 HOME Income Limits — Pennsylvania
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
source.method: Published Pittsburgh-area rows transcribed from the official PDF and checked against its extracted text. All four income-limit bands are published values, not percentages calculated from median family income.

caveats: These are HOME income-reference limits for the Pittsburgh HUD Metro FMR Area, including Allegheny County. They are not neighborhood median incomes or a forecast of new-construction rents.
Household size counts people, not bedrooms or homes. The table covers one through eight people; no other sizes are inferred.

HUD median family income is different from the parcel's ACS median household income. Published income limits include program adjustments; do not recreate them by multiplying the median by a percentage.
The HOME 30% row is not the Section 8 extremely-low-income row, which includes poverty-guideline adjustments and differs here for households of five or more.

A household budget calculated as 30% of annual income divided by 12 is a planning benchmark, not a published HOME or LIHTC rent limit. Program rents, bedroom rules, utility allowances, eligibility, covenants, financing and subsidies require separate review.

LIHTC and tax-exempt housing-bond projects use applicable MTSP limits and project-specific rules. The published Pittsburgh FY2026 MTSP 60% values match this HOME row, but that does not make the programs interchangeable.

relatedSources.name: HUD FY2026 MTSP Briefing Materials
relatedSources.note: Pages 3–4 explain the 60% calculation and hold-harmless rules; pages 9–10 describe rent restrictions and imputed household size.
